alt.text: 1,399 as of 15 Sep 2026 (NDRRMA SitRep #25/English #14). SitReps #26-28 were not read into this file.

5,985 before NDRRMA deducts the 110 bodies identified so far. The chart structure changed from #25: it now carries only two rows per district (local residents; people from other districts) plus a single foreign-nationals row of 636, rather than the extra Nepal Army/Police/government/bank-employee rows and the separate 49-worker Indian row carried in #25. Rasuwa is 1,677 local plus 1,836 from other districts (3,513); Nuwakot is 657 local plus 1,179 from other districts (1,836); foreign nationals are 636. The English #18 gives the identical chart.

Situation Report #18 publishes no injured count. Its nearest figure is "a total of 344 patients received treatment" across 19 hospitals as of 19 Sep, of whom 290 discharged, 18 still under treatment, 32 referred to other hospitals and 4 died during treatment - a cumulative treatment count, not the same category

series.note: Rescued includes 252 foreign nationals and 3,344 lifted by helicopter.

NDRRMA SitRep #01, 09:00 NPT. Bodies recovered from eight districts along the Bhote Koshi-Trishuli basin. Missing reported across 62 districts nationally. Rescued includes 253 foreign nationals and 3,702 lifted by helicopter. Injured is 279 treated across 16 facilities. OCHA Flash Update #5 and press reporting gave 1,003 dead for the same morning; the two are not reconciled.

NDRRMA SitRep #02. Missing stated as approximately 4,216, of which 583 (14%) foreign nationals and 164 DEOC-verified. 301 patients treated across 17 health facilities, 195 discharged, 70 still under treatment, 33 referred, 3 died in treatment. No injured count restated.

NDRRMA SitRep #03. Missing approximately 5,053: DEOC-verified 4,470 (88%) and 583 foreign nationals (12%); the bar chart gives Nuwakot 2,340 and Rasuwa 2,130. 304 treated, 70 still under treatment, 30 referred, 4 died in treatment. 4,521 people in 38 holding centres (Nuwakot 3,181 in 24, Dhading 199 in 3). The Nawalparasi West figure of 292 on this dashboard is anomalous against 202 the day before and 212 the day after, and is reproduced as printed.

NDRRMA SitRep #04. Missing chart unchanged from #03: 4,470 DEOC-verified, 583 foreign nationals, Nuwakot 2,340, Rasuwa 2,130. 1,085 people in 12 holding centres in Rasuwa, 2,572 in 25 in Nuwakot, 216 in 3 in Dhading.

NDRRMA SitRep #05, text figures. Missing approximately 4,896: DEOC-verified 4,307 (88%), 583 foreign nationals, Nuwakot 2,340, Rasuwa 1,967. 316 treated across 19 health facilities, 210 discharged, 72 still under treatment, 30 referred, 4 died in treatment. 3,912 people across 39 holding centres.

NDRRMA SitRep #06. Its dashboard page is still headed 5 September and its district and missing figures duplicate #05's - an apparent template carry-over in the source PDF, reproduced as printed. Rescued 13,391 and 323 treated (62 still under treatment, 30 referred) come from #06's own text. 3,533 people across 39 holding centres.
Missing stated as approximately 5,000, including about 600 foreign nationals from 35 countries. Rescued includes 300+ foreign nationals.

NDRRMA SitRep #07, 19:00 NPT. Missing approximately 4,894: DEOC-verified 4,307 (88%), 587 foreign nationals (12%), Nuwakot 2,340, Rasuwa 1,967, plus around 100 security personnel and government officials. 327 treated, 51 still under treatment, 30 referred. 3,629 people across 37 holding centres. MoFA's own update for the same day gave 1,355 recovered and about 5,000 missing; the two are not reconciled.

MoFA daily update, 14:00 NPT. Missing approximately 5,300 including about 600 foreign nationals from 35 countries; rescued includes 300+ foreign nationals. Confirms two Nepali tunnel survivors from Upper Trishuli 3A (4 Sep) and one Chinese national from Upper Trishuli 1 (5 Sep); SAR teams from India, China, South Korea, UAE, Malaysia and Australia active in tunnel rescue.
As of 18:00. No injured or rescued figure restated in this update.

NDRRMA spokesperson Shanti Mahat, 14:52 NPT, via Khabarhub. Missing decreased from the 8 Sep figure, consistent with reclassification from missing to recovered rather than a data error. 102 bodies identified and returned to families; 3,628 people in holding centres across Nuwakot, Dhading, Rasuwa and Kathmandu; 7,151 people received medical treatment, a broader/cumulative figure not the same category as the 279 injured figure from 1 Sep.

NDRRMA SitRep #09 (English) and SitRep #19 (Nepali), which carry identical figures. Missing 5,132 after deducting the 102 bodies identified by then; the chart splits Rasuwa 2,860 (local residents 1,393, people from other districts 1,286, Nepal Army 45, Nepal Police 25, Armed Police Force 12, government employees 73, bank and financial-institution employees 26) and Nuwakot 1,787 (651 local, 1,136 from other districts), with 587 foreign nationals carried separately. 333 treated, 42 still under treatment. 34 holding centres. NDRRMA's spokesperson gave 1,367 and 5,132 the same afternoon via Khabarhub; the SitRep's 1,369 is two higher.

NDRRMA SitRep #22, 19:00 NPT. 339 patients treated across 19 health facilities, 269 discharged, 34 still under treatment, 32 referred, 4 died in treatment; a further 8,615 treated by the security agencies. 1,482 Nepal Army flights and 320 Armed Police Force flights. Holding centres are stated twice and disagree: the dashboard gives 37 centres sheltering 3,761 (Nuwakot 2,587, Rasuwa 839, Dhading 335) while the text gives 36 centres and 3,434 (Nuwakot 2,502 in 25, Rasuwa 839 in 9, Dhading 93 in 2). The Kathmandu Post reported the same 1,386 and 5,130 that day.

NDRRMA SitRep #23, 19:00 NPT. Missing is 5,234 on the chart less the 104 bodies identified so far. The 1,388 recovered break down as 542 male, 334 female and 512 partial remains; 1,286 DNA samples have been taken from the deceased and 1,846 from relatives. 339 treated across 19 health facilities, 271 discharged, 32 still under treatment, 32 referred, 4 died in treatment; a further 9,314 treated by the security agencies. 1,516 Nepal Army flights (34 on the day) and 320 Armed Police Force flights.

NDRRMA SitRep #24, 19:00 NPT. Missing is 5,234 on the chart less the 104 bodies identified so far, unchanged for a third day. The deceased breakdown still reads 542 male, 334 female and 512 partial remains, which sums to the 1,388 of the day before rather than the new 1,395; the district bars do sum to 1,395. DNA samples stand at 1,286 from the deceased and 1,853 from relatives. 341 treated across 19 health facilities, 278 discharged, 27 still under treatment, 32 referred, 4 died in treatment; a further 9,358 treated by the security agencies. 1,531 Nepal Army flights (15 on the day) and 320 Armed Police Force flights.

NDRRMA SitRep #25 (Nepali) and #14 (English), 19:00 NPT. Missing rises for the first time since 9 September, from 5,130 to 5,179, because the chart gains a row it did not previously carry - 49 Indian nationals working at hydropower projects - taking the chart total from 5,234 to 5,283 against the same 104 identified bodies deducted; no pre-existing row moved. The deceased breakdown is corrected to 544 male, 336 female and 519 partial remains, which sums to the new 1,399, resolving the mismatch printed in #24, and the district bars sum to 1,399 as well. DNA samples stand at 1,286 from the deceased and 1,889 from relatives. 343 treated across 19 health facilities, 282 discharged, 25 still under treatment, 32 referred, 4 died in treatment; a further 9,496 treated by the security agencies. 1,561 Nepal Army flights (30 on the day) and 320 Armed Police Force flights. Holding centres fall to 30 sheltering 2,155 people.

NDRRMA SitRep #29 (Nepali) and #18 (English), 19:00 NPT, four days after #25/#14 (SitReps #26-28 were not read into this file). Missing falls to 5,875 from 5,179 on 15 Sep: the chart is restructured to carry only local-residents and other-district rows per district plus one merged foreign-nationals row of 636 (previously 587 plus a separate 49-worker row), and 110 identified bodies are now deducted rather than 104. The deceased breakdown is 549 male, 336 female and 526 partial remains, summing to the new 1,411. DNA samples stand at 1,286 from the deceased; the report gives 1,991 for relatives on its infographic and 1,997 in its own text, not reconciled here. 344 treated across 19 health facilities, 290 discharged, 18 still under treatment, 32 referred, 4 died in treatment; a further 10,041 treated by the security agencies. 1,692 Nepal Army flights and 320 Armed Police Force flights. Holding centres fall to 24 sheltering 1,342 people (Rasuwa 794 in 9, Nuwakot 427 in 11, Dhading 121 in 4). The Rasuwa District Security Committee stood down further search and rescue at Langtang and Chilime; at Upper Trishuli-1's Adit-3 tunnel, 31 bodies were recovered (plus 6 recovered earlier).

china.detail: Gyirong (Kyirong) county, Tibet Autonomous Region. Missing includes about 261 foreign nationals. Xinhua reported 31 dead and 531 missing as of 4 September.
china.note: Tracked entirely separately from Nepal's national count. No NDRRMA or MoFA figure includes these people.

foreign_nationals.detail: NDRRMA's missing chart now carries a single foreign-nationals row of 636, replacing the 587-plus-a-separate-49-worker split carried in SitRep #25 of 15 September (SitReps #26-28 were not read into this file, so the exact point of the merge is not established). The English #18 gives the same 636.

alternates.label: Nepal Tourism Board
alternates.detail: 644 travellers unaccounted for in total: 517 foreign nationals and 127 Nepalis.

foreign_nationals.note: NDRRMA's own 587 now matches the Department of Tourism count taken a week earlier; MoFA's ~600 and the Nepal Tourism Board's 644 were taken on different dates by different agencies and have not been reconciled. India is the largest single nationality reported, revised upward from 178 to 288 across updates.

notes: The headline figure is bodies recovered, not identified deaths. NDRRMA SitRep #29 of 19 September puts formally identified bodies at 110 of 1,411, and subtracts exactly those 110 from the missing total; forensic teams from India, China, Japan, Singapore and South Korea have been working since early September.

Missing is a separate category and is not presumed dead. NDRRMA notes on every dashboard that the out-of-contact figure may still include unidentified bodies and people already rescued, and that it is being verified.

District counts reflect where a body was found, not where the person lived or died. Bodies travelled up to 240 km downstream, which is why Chitwan (364, unchanged since 13 September) and the two Nawalparasi districts (454 combined, unchanged) show higher recovered-body counts than the upstream epicentre districts of Rasuwa (199) and Nuwakot (203).
The often-quoted ~900 figure is the 31 August snapshot, not a competing method. It is the same count at an earlier date.

NDRRMA publishes a situation report every day, and the Nepali and English editions are numbered separately: the Nepali #29 and the English #18 are both dated 19 September 2026, 19:00 NPT, and their dashboards carry identical figures. Nepali #20 (10 Sep) and #21 (11 Sep) were never posted to the Rasuwa index and their /mediafiles/rasuwa/ URLs return 404, but both are in the general publication index at /api/v1/publication/publications/ under /mediafiles/publications/, which is where every edition from 10 September on is filed. The English #12 of 13 September and #13 of 14 September carry "Situation Report # 11" on their inner pages, a template slip; the English #14 corrects it. SitReps #26, #27 and #28 (Nepali) and their English equivalents were not read into this file, so this bump moves directly from #25/#14 (15 Sep) to #29/#18 (19 Sep).

No consolidated official injured count has been published since 31 August 2026. SitRep #29 reports 344 patients treated across 19 health facilities and 10,041 treated by the security agencies, both cumulative treatment counts in a different category from the 279 injured figure of 1 September, and neither replaces it.

The missing breakdown is published only as an infographic, and its structure changed in this edition. Read off SitRep #29's chart it is: Rasuwa 1,677 local residents plus 1,836 people from other districts (3,513), Nuwakot 657 local plus 1,179 from other districts (1,836), and a single foreign-nationals row of 636 - the Nepal Army, Nepal Police, government-employee and bank-employee rows carried separately through SitRep #25, and the extra 49-worker Indian hydropower row introduced in #25, no longer appear as such (SitReps #26-28 were not read into this file, so the exact point of the change is not established). Those figures sum to 5,985, from which NDRRMA subtracts the 110 identified bodies to reach 5,875. It gives no equivalent Rasuwa/Nuwakot split of the dead.

NDRRMA's initial damage and needs assessment, published in SitRep #22 on 12 September and not repeated in #23, puts 32,936 people, 8,317 households and 7,570 private buildings affected; 13 hydropower plants, 69 km of road, 68 suspension bridges, 37 motorable bridges and 443 km of pipeline damaged; 48 public buildings, 30 heritage sites, 18 schools and 7 health facilities in the social sector; 1,806 ha of cropland, 697.05 ha of irrigated agriculture, 4,800 business establishments and 17 bank branches; total disaster effect Rs 408 bn against total recovery needs of Rs 723 bn, of which Rs 8.73 bn immediate. It names Bidur (Nuwakot), Gosaikunda (Rasuwa), Benighat Rorang (Dhading) and Kispang (Nuwakot) as the four worst-affected local levels, with 3,431, 1,156, 1,146 and 721 respectively - the graphic does not state what those numbers count, so they are not carried into the municipality table. The detailed PDNA is still in progress.

Cash relief was extended on 10 September 2026 by cabinet decision to households whose homes were destroyed across 15 local levels in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Tanahun and Gorkha: Rs 15,000 a month for a household of up to four, plus Rs 2,000 a month per further member, for up to six months or until alternative accommodation is arranged, and only for families housing themselves rather than staying in a holding centre. Situation reports through #29 publish no district or local-level total of what has actually been disbursed.
IOM appealed on 8 September for USD 20.5 million to assist 43,000 of an estimated 84,000 people affected by the floods, as part of the Government of Nepal-led response.

summary.text: Ready-to-eat food delivered; rice, lentils and solar batteries still required. Named with Aamachhodingmo as one of the two most severely affected local levels: 3,702 households and 14,461 people isolated for up to six days, of them 3,650 children and 1,204 older people. Syafrubesi and Timure health posts and the Timure health desk were fully damaged.

households_isolated.detail: Combined figure for Gosaikunda and Aamachhodingmo together

people_isolated.detail: Combined figure for Gosaikunda and Aamachhodingmo together

summary.text: Ready-to-eat food delivered; rice, lentils and solar batteries still required. All wards were cut off from the road network and ward 1 was directly flood-hit. Only ward 1 had grid power by 6 September, with four wards still dark.

wards_official.text: All wards cut off from the road network; ward 1 directly flood-affected

summary.text: Minimum food supplies had reached; a shortage of tents was causing shelter difficulties, with rice, lentils and solar batteries still required. The Mailung Community Health Unit was fully damaged, and the Trishuli-Mailung-Syabrubesi road at Khalte in ward 5 was completely and persistently obstructed.
Ready-to-eat food delivered to all locations; rice, lentils and solar batteries still required.

Disinfectant and chemicals were needed to control the odour from dead animals and human remains. Twenty-four bodies were found in a single house at Betrawati in ward 10; between Sole Bazar and Akkare Bazar in ward 7 houses were washed away, two concrete bridges destroyed and more than 200 residents were out of contact. The Bidur water supply project lost 4.5 km of pipeline and three sump wells, affecting about 4,000 households, and a wastewater treatment plant was destroyed.
Four holding centres were open. The Pasang Lhamu road at Simtar in ward 10 was completely obstructed. Site of the Trishuli Galchhi project. No municipality-level casualty figure was published.
No shelter facilities and no relief had reached the municipality. Immediate relief was needed at Belkotgadhi, Mahadevsthan and Ratamate.

Minimum essential supplies available, but road access and electricity were unresolved. The municipality requested 50 to 60 solar units, was procuring its own medical supplies, and asked for the rest by helicopter.
Two bridges on the Tadi Khola were destroyed.

Drinking water needed. The Prithvi Highway is fully blocked at Krishnabhir, where about 70 m of road foundation collapsed into the Trishuli, and again at Parewabhir; the Mugling-Kathmandu section is closed both directions. About half of a 300 m bypass track had opened by early September before new slope cracks were found above the worksite. The Phurke Khola bridge at Malekhu was also washed away.

Three hundred metres of 50 mm pipe was needed to restore drinking water to about 100 households in ward 1. Baireni Hospital was partially damaged. The municipality is also the hub of the reopened right-bank detour to Trishuli Bazar.
Downstream municipality on the Trishuli. No municipality-level figure published; Chitwan's 363 recovered bodies are a district total and reflect where remains were found, not local deaths.
Downstream municipality on the Narayani. No municipality-level figure published.
The Tokha-Chhahare road at Ghattekhola in ward 8 was placed under a 22:00 to 05:00 night restriction.

Right bank of the Trishuli opposite Dhading; touched by the observed flood extent (HOT, 27 Aug imagery). No official municipality-level figure published; Gorkha district recorded 65 bodies recovered as of 1 Sep (NDRRMA), 75 as of 8 Sep.

Right bank of the Trishuli opposite Dhading; touched by the observed flood extent (HOT, 27 Aug imagery). No official municipality-level figure published; Gorkha district recorded 65 bodies recovered as of 1 Sep (NDRRMA), 75 as of 8 Sep.

Deaths during treatment in Kathmandu hospitals, listed as a separate bar on NDRRMA’s chart alongside the eight river-corridor districts; first appears in SitRep #09 of 9 September

generation_offline.note: Mongabay reports 281 MW for the same period; a 550 MW figure circulates but is uncorroborated.

under_construction.note: Combined operating plus under-construction capacity affected is cited as 748 MW: 9 operating projects at 354 MW plus 5 under construction at 394 MW.

projects_damaged.note: NDRRMA names 13 facilities. Press counts vary from 12 to 14.

capacity_affected.note: NDRRMA SitRep #01, combined capacity of the 13 named damaged facilities. Press reporting gives 748 MW for a similar basis; the two are not reconciled.

projects.name: Upper Trishuli-1
projects.owner: Korea South-East Power (lead, 50%) with Doosan Enerbility; NWEDC
projects.what: More than 90% of the upper dam destroyed; about 90% of base-camp housing destroyed.
projects.workers_missing: 576 reported missing at the site, about 300 believed trapped in the tunnel; 6 Doosan Enerbility staff and 3 of 7 Korea South-East Power construction-management staff unaccounted for.
projects.note: Search and rescue ongoing, 13 Sep: water is flowing out of the Audit-3 tunnel, raising the risk of going further in. At Audit-1 in Hakubeshi a team of 5 Nepal Army personnel with project representatives searched 200 m in and found nothing; 1 Nepal Army member and 9 Australians worked Audit-3.

projects.name: Rasuwagadhi
projects.what: Headworks and dam completely washed away, per the NEA spokesperson.
projects.workers_missing: Not itemised separately; folded into the aggregate counts.
projects.note: Search and rescue ongoing, 13 Sep: heavy equipment is needed but hard to move in on the terrain; a joint team of 5 Nepalis and 4 Australian DART members searched and returned. NDRRMA lists this project at 120 MW rather than the 111 MW carried here.

projects.name: Super Trishuli
projects.what: Named by NDRRMA among the 13 damaged facilities. Spotlight Nepal reported it as unaffected, about 100 km downstream of Betrawati Bazar; the two accounts conflict and NDRRMA is taken as the official one here.
projects.note: Damage status conflicts between NDRRMA and press reporting.

projects.name: Upper Trishuli-3A
projects.what: Tunnel flooded; workers trapped in the main tunnel, two pulled out alive on day nine.
projects.workers_missing: 42 workers reported missing; about 557 unaccounted for at the wider Mailung site, 115 believed trapped in the main tunnel.
projects.note: Search and rescue ongoing, 13 Sep: continuous rainfall triggered landslides around the entrance tunnel to the 3A powerhouse, blocking the mouth; clearance is under way. NDRRMA calls this project Trishuli 3A (60 MW).

projects.name: Sanjen
projects.note: Capacity reported as both 42.5 MW and 78 MW.

projects.name: Upper Trishuli-3B
projects.what: The associated 220 kV Trishuli 3B hub substation was completely destroyed, buried under landslide debris.
projects.note: Search and rescue ongoing, 13 Sep: searching down to the depth of the project’s residential quarters. The riverbed is at 653 m above sea level and excavation has reached 651 m without finding structural remains of the building. NDRRMA calls this project Trishuli 3B (37 MW).

projects.name: Trishuli
projects.what: Riverbank transmission lines and substations destroyed.

projects.name: Chilime
projects.workers_missing: 133 employees reported missing on 1 September; a later update put 6 trapped in the tunnel. Counts were revised down as contact and rescue progressed.
projects.note: Search and rescue ongoing, 13 Sep: rocky terrain was blasted to bring heavy equipment to the tunnel and 85 m of access track completed; debris has been cleared about 70 m into the tunnel. Tunnel breakthrough and road clearance are being done jointly by the Nepal Army and the Indian Army, with 15 Nepal Army and 12 Indian personnel including NDRF working inside the tunnel.

projects.name: Langtang Khola
projects.note: Search and rescue ongoing, 13 Sep: soil and large rocks are being cleared from an entrance about 10 m long, 3 ft wide and 4 ft high on the route leading from the outlet to the other side. A search inside the tunnel found nothing.

projects.name: Devighat
projects.what: Completely wiped out; the furthest downstream plant damage cited.

projects.name: Mailung Khola
projects.status_before: Sources differ, operating or under construction
projects.what: Lost both the powerhouse and the headworks.
projects.note: Capacity reported as both 5 MW and 14.8 MW.

projects.name: Upper Trishuli-2
projects.what: Named by NDRRMA among the 13 damaged facilities; no detail published.

grid.detail: Completely destroyed and buried under landslide debris. Not restored as of the latest reporting, and cited as a key evacuation bottleneck.
Used by NEA to reroute power, stepped down to 11 kV for local feeders. Active and carrying emergency restoration load.
Not detailed in the sources checked; damage is implied by the destruction of the Chilime powerhouse but no figure was published.
Rasuwagadhi, Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi, Chilime, Langtang Khola, Upper Trishuli 1, 2, 3A and 3B, Mailung Khola, Middle Trishuli Ganga, Trishuli, Devighat and Super Trishuli.

restoration.note: Nepal Energy Forum gives 83% for the same date; the two are not reconciled.
OnlineKhabar separately reports about 90% for the same date.
About 120 families still without power. The Kathmandu Post described this as nearly all households on 6 September.

restoration.detail: 500 portable 2 kW household solar units and 13 institutional solar systems distributed through the Alternative Energy Promotion Centre; 1,268 vulnerable Rasuwa households flagged for solar.

restoration.note: Ministry of Energy figure, confirming Nepal Energy Forum's earlier 83% reading (vs Kathmandu Post's 78% for 6 September, also in this table).
Ministry of Energy figure. Lower than the 96.7% reported for 6 September; likely a denominator or rounding difference between agencies rather than a real regression — not reconciled.

The last ward restored in Nuwakot. NDRRMA SitRep #19 declares the district covered with this connection, while noting that some flood-hit households remain without supply. No percentage is given. The electricity section disappeared from the reports after #19 and returned with the English #13 of 14 September.

Approximately 90% of households, up from about 80% on 14 September. 738 households in Uttargaya wards 1 and 2 and Gosaikunda wards 1, 2 and 3 remain without supply; supply was extended to further areas of Aamachhodingmo ward 1 and Gosaikunda ward 5. Coordination continues to feed 170 households in Gosaikunda ward 3 from the 100 kW Langtang micro-hydropower plant in ward 4 once local agreement is reached.

restoration.detail: Restored district-wide except the flood-hit Betrawati area
restoration.note: Supplied from Chapali and Balaju in Kathmandu, with low voltage still a problem and a technical assessment underway to bring the Devighat substation into operation. No percentage is given.
The Jahare substation is operational, resolving the low-voltage problem. No percentage is given.

impact.text: Nepal became a net electricity exporter for the first time in about a decade in the fiscal year ending mid-July 2026, earning Rs 18.75 bn from sales to India and Bangladesh. Officials expect that to reverse in the winter low-flow season and have sought advance import approvals from India effective September 2026.
India agreed to supply advance power to Nepal to cope with the flood, ahead of the normal schedule.

Loss estimates diverge sharply. IPPAN puts hydropower-sector losses at Rs 25-30 bn, roughly a quarter to a third of affected project costs; NEA's preliminary assessment says hundreds of billions of rupees; the Finance Minister attributed Rs 100 bn specifically to hydro infrastructure within a Rs 900 bn economy-wide rebuilding figure.

Missing-worker counts across the energy sector were revised sharply downward as rescue and contact efforts progressed: 933 (NDRRMA), 898 at 11 projects (IPPAN, 29 August), 983 out of contact against 639 officially counted missing, and by 7 September the Nepal Army believed 121 people were still trapped in hydropower tunnels.

road.detail: Betrawati-Rasuwagadhi road (42 km) destroyed at multiple points; no reopening date and authorities advise against travel.
Miteri Friendship Bridge and the border customs post destroyed on 26 August.
16 km section toward the China border damaged; market area flood-hit on 26 August. A 75 m Bailey bridge span is needed here.
Bogatitar-Kalikasthan-Dhunche section reopened to light four-wheel-drive only; the Bidur-Dhunche road was limited to small 4WD vehicles.

displacement_site.detail: Relief supplies staged here; onward delivery to villages is the bottleneck.

road.detail: Passable in daylight only, with a mandatory night closure enforced. (unofficial)
Trishuli-Mailung-Syabrubesi road washed away; helicopter access only for relief.
Roads to Simle and Shanti Bazaar wiped out; no access to shops, hospitals or government offices.

Bailey bridge not yet started as of 8-9 Sep; the Nepal Army bridging team is due to move to Betrawati immediately after finishing Devighat. About 1.5 km of track remains to be opened between Dhunge Bazar and Betrawati before installation can begin.

power.detail: Not reported separately from the Nuwakot district figure.

road.detail: Old and new Trishuli Bazar bridges swept away. A 48 m Bailey bridge is planned but not yet installed.

telecom.detail: Ncell tower still down in the Trishuli/Bidur area.

road.detail: Reachable via the reopened Galchhi detour; the direct Trishuli-Betrawati road is still damaged.

water.detail: Bidur Water Supply Project running on a 100 kVA diesel generator, distributing about 500,000 litres a day. A short-term measure, not a restoration.

road.detail: Nepal Army-built 60 m Acrow bridge over the Tadi river (5.5 m wide, 50-tonne capacity, built in five days by a 55-member Bridging Unit team) opened to pedestrians from 10 Sep; vehicle traffic due to resume from 11 Sep.
Terminus of the Galchhi detour route toward Trishuli Bazar; open as a narrow single-lane track.
Hub of the reopened right-bank detour road, the alternative to the destroyed Trishuli-corridor bridges.
Phurke Khola bridge washed away, with local road damage.

Prithvi Highway fully blocked at Krishnabhir by a 70 m road-foundation collapse into the Trishuli; the Muglin-Kathmandu section is closed both ways. About 50 m of a 300 m bypass track had opened before new slope cracks were found above the worksite.
All wards reported inaccessible by road.

power.detail: Only ward 1 has power; four wards remain dark.

corridor.text: Pasang Lhamu Highway (NH42), Betrawati to Rasuwagadhi: 42 km damaged at multiple points with several concrete bridges washed away, plus a further 16 km from Syabrubesi toward the China border. No confirmed reopening date; authorities advise against travel to Rasuwagadhi, Timure or Kerung until the route is reassessed.

NDRRMA listed ten obstructed road sections on 1 September: the Prithvi Highway completely blocked at Krishnabhir and Parewabhir on the Mugling-Dhading section and blocked again on Mugling-Malekhu; Galchhi-Devighat and Devighat-Dhunge blocked; the Trishuli-Mailung-Syabrubesi road completely and persistently obstructed at Khalte in Uttargaya-5; all main highways in Rasuwa closed until further notice; the Pasang Lhamu road completely obstructed at Simtar in Belkotgadhi-10; night restrictions on the Tokha-Chhahare road at Ghattekhola in Shivapuri-8 and on the B.P. Highway in Kavre; and the Kanti Lokpath blocked by a landslide at Bhattedanda in Lalitpur.

Prithvi Highway is closed both directions at Krishnabhir in Benighat Rorang, Dhading, where about 70 m of road foundation collapsed into the Trishuli. A 300 m bypass track is under construction, roughly half open, but seven cracks up to 15 m long were found in the slope above the worksite. The Prime Minister said the section would reopen within September.

Detour in use: Galchhi to Kalleritar, Koshikhola, Piplatar, Darshantar, Chhatrekhola and Gauribesi along the right bank of the Trishuli. It restores a rough single-lane connection from Dhading and Galchhi to Trishuli Bazar without crossing the destroyed river bridges, but is narrow, slow and hard for two-way traffic.

Bailey bridges planned by the Department of Roads at four locations: Devighat in Bidur, where the Nepal Army has begun installation; Trishuli Bazaar and Betrawati, each needing about a 48 m span; and Syabrubesi, needing about 75 m. Moving the components is hampered because the lower road sections are still blocked. China has supplied Bailey components at the Korala border for possible use at Rasuwagadhi.

Named bridges destroyed: Betrawati old and new; the Trishuli River bridge at Tupche; Trishuli Bazar old and new; Simchaur; the bridge near the Water Resources and Irrigation Division at Devighat; a Mid-Hill Highway bridge; two on the Tadi Khola; Shreekali, Budhsinghghat, Ratamate and Phosretar over the Trishuli; and in Dhading the Syaltar road bridge, Ghatbesi bridge, Phurke Khola bridge at Malekhu and two on the Kolpu Khola.

Bridge totals are not reconciled across sources. NDRRMA reported 41 motorable bridges washed away and 4 more damaged; OnlineKhabar counted at least 19 bridges and about 40 km of road along the Trishuli corridor; the Department of Roads early estimate was 68 suspension and 33 driveable bridges damaged, with an initial Rs 15 bn estimate for road and bridge infrastructure.

Electricity, district level: Rasuwa 78% of 14,281 affected households restored, Nuwakot 96.7% of 68,679, Dhading 99.8% of 83,642 with about 120 families still dark. Rasuwa floods affected roughly 10% of Nepal's total generation capacity.

Water supply: 55 drinking-water projects damaged across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Gorkha, with Rs 640 m estimated damage; Nuwakot is worst hit with 22 projects affected. The Bidur Water Supply Project runs on a 100 kVA diesel generator distributing about 500,000 litres a day.

UNICEF reported at least 22,000 children in the flood-affected areas without safe drinking water, sanitation and hygiene support, and dispatched supplies for about 19,000 people in Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

Telecommunications: Nepal Telecom restored 116 of 120 affected towers by 1 September using helicopter-carried crews. Ncell restored 24 of 27, leaving Ghattekhola and Timure in Rasuwa and Trishuli/Bidur in Nuwakot down; 60 km of fibre was damaged and total telecom infrastructure damage is put at Rs 450 m.

Displacement: 3,458 people were living in 27 displacement sites in Nuwakot and Rasuwa, mostly in schools, as of 1 September. IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix covers 15 sites in Dhading, Nuwakot and Rasuwa and estimates 4,288 households affected, of which 2,886 displaced.

Cross-border: the Gyirong checkpoint on the Chinese side was destroyed, along with a 5 km stretch of China National Highway 216 toward Rasuwagadhi, and communications and power to the Gyirong Port area were cut. About 80 trucks and 170 containers were stranded in Gyirong town. On the Nepal side the Rasuwagadhi customs office was destroyed and more than 300 vehicles plus roughly 1,000 electric vehicles awaiting export were swept away.

Health facilities: Syafrubesi and Timure health posts, the Timure health desk and the Mailung community health unit were fully damaged; Baireni Hospital in Galchhi and the Charadhuli basic health service centre were partially damaged; access to Dhading and Trishuli hospitals was disrupted. Nineteen schools were surveyed across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, covering 6,901 enrolled students: eight fully damaged, eight partially damaged, three safe.

Shelter: 30 holding centres held 3,930 people, 19 centres and 2,653 people in Nuwakot and 11 centres and 1,277 people in Rasuwa. In Nuwakot 1,267 houses were fully damaged and 1,253 partially damaged. Satellite mapping put 4,689 buildings inside the flood zone, an exposure estimate rather than verified damage.

Nuwakot agriculture, preliminary: 4,440 ropani of crops affected, 2,035 livestock and 16,500 birds lost. Two wastewater treatment plants were destroyed at Dhunge and Bidur, and 465 further households were affected across the Trishuli Colony, Devighat and Betrawati water schemes.

Krishnabhir remains fully closed on the Prithvi Highway (about 300 m of road collapsed on 30 August). Department of Roads Director General Bijaya Jaisi said a decision on whether vehicles can pass through will come within a week. Two long-term bypass options are under study: twin 500 m tunnels, or two permanent bridges rerouting the highway across the Trishuli River and back, with repairing the existing road the first priority. Two detours are in use: a Galchhi route via a bridge near "Hamlet Restaurant" along the opposite riverbank (about 20 km, to Parewatar), and a Chitwan-side route via the Fishling and Benighat bridges (about 17.5 km, with a 1.5 km stretch still under repair).

Bidur-Betrawati, 13 September: 9.2 km of the 10 km section is clear; the remaining 0.8 km was washed away entirely and a new track is being cut, including 0.5 km through hard rock, with gravelling started. Landslide and bog problems persist on both the new and old tracks. Foundation excavation has started for a Bailey bridge at Betrawati. The Acrow bridge at Devighat in Nuwakot is installed and carrying traffic. Devighat-Dhunge and Dhunge-Trishuli are fully clear. Prithvi Highway remains completely blocked at Krishnabhir on the Mugling-Malekhu section, where a 250 m hillside track has been opened and gravelling begun; three signed detours to Kathmandu run via Arughat and Dhadingbesi. Tribhuvan Highway is single-lane past landslides at Nagdhunga and Pataleban, with traffic moving through the Nagdhunga tunnel.

About 40 km of road was destroyed outright between Nuwakot and Rasuwa and 41 motorable bridges between Rasuwa and Dhading, leaving the Rasuwagadhi road facing long repairs. India has sent three 70 m Bailey bridges. The target is a temporary track through to the border before Dashain.

Telecommunications, 13 September: Nepal Telecom has 117 of 120 BTS towers operating and Ncell 76 of 78. Ten of 29 satellite internet terminals are installed and working, six in Nuwakot and four in Rasuwa. Service is still down at Chilime Khola, Trishuli 3B and Uttargaya-1 (Tiru) for lack of electricity.

Isolated settlements, 12 September: Thuman (Gosaikunda ward 1), Langtang (Gosaikunda ward 4) and Chilime (Aamachhodingmo ward 5) still have no road access and were supplied by helicopter with 8.28 t of rice, lentils, oil and salt, reaching 227 households so far. A further 354 affected families in Kalika RM (Rasuwa) and Tarkeshwar RM (Nuwakot) received food. Of 20 repairable suspension bridges, 5 are under repair and 15 being prepared, with one new bridge started at Trishuli-Buddha Gumba.

Shelter, 13 September: 2,532 people remain in 33 holding centres - 1,613 in 22 centres in Nuwakot, 825 in 9 in Rasuwa and 94 in 2 in Dhading. That is down from 3,761 in 37 centres the day before, as families take up the cabinet’s 10 September cash-relief offer of Rs 15,000 a month (plus Rs 2,000 per member above four) for up to six months to arrange their own accommodation. Fuel stocks stand at 33,000 l of diesel, 18,000 l of petrol and 15,000 l of aviation fuel, with 502 LPG cylinders sent so far.

Monitoring: after the Bhote Koshi flood, and for the first time in Nepal, a CCTV camera has been installed at Timure about 70 m above the river and fed live into the 24-hour flood-forecasting service of the Centre for Hydrology and Water Resources Research.

Prithvi Highway, Mugling-Malekhu: completely obstructed at Krishnabhir by toe cutting. A 250 m track has been excavated on the hillside and graveling has commenced; work has started on an alternative route through Fisling Bridge to Benighat Bridge. At Shital Bazaar the road has subsided and runs one-way. Three signed alternative routes to Kathmandu run from Abukhaireni via Arughat, two of them through Dhadingbesi.
Tribhuvan Highway: obstructed by landslides near Nagdhunga and Pataleban and operating one-way; traffic has resumed through the Nagdhunga Tunnel.

Galchhi-Devighat-Dhunge-Trishuli: debris and mud near Thuli Khola cleared and traffic resumed on the Galchhi-Devighat section, with back cutting ongoing at Ratamate using two additional heavy machines; Kolphu Bridge carries one lane after minor repairs. Devighat-Dhunge and Dhunge-Trishuli are both operational and clear.

An Acrow bridge over the Tadi River at Devighat, on the Galchhi-Trishuli road section, is installed and in operation; the remaining launching nose, parts and accessories are being stored at the No. 1 Military Training Centre. Debris removal continues with 3 excavators, 3 backhoe loaders and 3 tippers at Devighat, 3 excavators, 2 backhoe loaders and 2 tippers at Dhunge, and 2 excavators and 1 tipper at Galchhi.

Alternative routes: Dhadingbesi-Parewatar-Nepaltar-Gajuritar-Piplatar-Adamtar-Belintar-Keurinatar-Mastar rejoins the Prithvi Highway and has reconnected Dhading’s district headquarters to the road network. For Rasuwa, with the Trishuli-Betrawati section damaged, the Dhikure (Mid-Hill Highway)-Phedi Besi Chowk-Hiramunitar-Chogte-Bore Bhanjyang-Sano Khola-Dhanswara-Bhorle-Jibjibe-Bogatitar route onto the Pasang Lhamu Highway is under maintenance, with vehicular movement to resume once track rehabilitation and graveling are done. The Devighat Bridge is bypassed via Pipaltar-Pasang Lhamu Highway-Dhamle-Niranjana-Bagkhor-Harre-Deurali-Kolputar, and Nuwakot across the Trishuli is reached from Galchhi over the Trishuli Bridge via Kalleritar, Koshikhola, Pimaltar, Darshantar, Chhatre Khola and Gauribesi to Trishuli Bazaar; both are operational with repairs ongoing.

Shelter, 14 September: 2,418 people remain in 33 holding centres - 1,499 in 22 centres in Nuwakot, 825 in 9 in Rasuwa and 94 in 2 in Dhading, down from 2,532 the day before. Site surveys for temporary shelter land are complete at Bidur and Belkotgadhi in Nuwakot, Galchi and Gajuri in Dhading, and in Rasuwa; structured camps with water, power, health and access are planned within two weeks and transitional shelters in four to ten. Fuel stocks stand at about 47,000 l of diesel (the Nepali edition prints 46,000), 16,000 l of petrol and 11,000 l of aviation fuel, with 502 LPG cylinders sent so far and 150 more dispatched to the Rasuwa district administration.

Bridges, 14 September: installation of the Bailey bridge at Devighat over the Tadi River is fully complete, and the Acrow bridge at Devighat in Nuwakot is in operation. Foundation construction has commenced for the Bailey bridge at Betrawati over the Phalakhu Khola.

Electricity, 14 September: Dhading is fully restored across the district, with the Jaharsab substation brought into service to clear low-voltage problems. Nuwakot is supplied from Chapali and Balaju in Kathmandu and restored everywhere except the flood-hit areas of Betrawati, with technical teams studying how to bring the Devighat substation back; a stabiliser was fitted for the Bidur water-supply pumps and a 3.36 kW solar system installed at Trishuli Hospital. Rasuwa is at about 80% of households, and the district administration is seeking local agreement to extend supply to Gosaikunda ward 3 from the 100 kW Langtang micro-hydro plant.

Rasuwa access, 14 September: with the Trishuli-Betrawati section still obstructed, vehicles reach Rasuwa via Dhikure on the Mid-Hill Highway, then Phedibesi, Chogate, Bore Bhanjyang, Bhorle, Jibjibe and Bogatitar onto the Pasang Lhamu Highway. Traffic from Kaski, Lamjung, Tanahun and Gorkha now enters Kathmandu via Abukhaireni, 12 Kilo, Masanethanti, Arughat, Salyantar and Dhadingbesi.

Search and rescue, 14 September: operations are still open at every hydropower site. A joint Nepali Army and Chinese DART team went about 170 m into the Langtang tunnel with a thermal drone and found nothing; at Upper Trishuli-1 a team searched 200 m into the Audit-1 tunnel at Hakubesi with no trace, while water gushing from Audit-3 is raising the risk of further entry. Chilime is cleared about 90 m in and being entered on ropes under a 1.5 to 2 ft gap. At Trishuli 3B, excavation about 2 m below the riverbed found the foundation of the project office but nothing of residential blocks A1, A2, B1, B2 or D. A CQRT and project team reached the Rasuwagadhi powerhouse, transformer room and control room. Search, drone and K9 deployment is now complete along the 218 km river corridor from Timure to Triveni across 8 districts.

Shelter, 15 September: 2,155 people remain in 30 holding centres - 1,236 in 19 centres in Nuwakot, 825 in 9 in Rasuwa and 94 in 2 in Dhading, down from 2,418 in 33 centres the day before. Fuel stocks on the dashboard stand at about 39,000 l of diesel, 10,000 l of petrol and 9,000 l of aviation fuel, with 502 LPG cylinders sent so far and 150 of them to the Rasuwa district administration. The report's own text separately states that 145,000 l of aviation fuel has been supplied in total with 10,000 l remaining at the Nuwakot barracks, which does not match the 9,000 l on the dashboard; both are reproduced as printed.

Roads, 15 September: the Prithvi Highway remains blocked at Krishnabhir, where graveling of the newly cut 250 m track is nearing completion but traffic has not resumed, and the proposed Fisling-to-Benighat bridge alternative is still in procurement with construction not begun; road subsidence at Shital Bazaar has cut traffic to one lane. On the Galchhi-Devighat section, hillside cutting at Ratamate is finished and traffic has resumed, with Kolphu bridge open to one lane. Of the 10 km Bidur-Betrawati section, 9.2 km is clear and the remaining 0.8 km was washed away entirely, with 0.5 km of hard rock still being cut. The Dhikure-Jibjibe-Bogatitar route into Rasuwa is operational.

Bridges, 15 September: an Acrow bridge at Devighat in Nuwakot has been installed and brought into operation. Foundation excavation is underway for a Bailey bridge at Betrawati. A roughly 30 m temporary footbridge at Betrawati, Bidur-10 on the Nuwakot-Rasuwa border, built on Bhadra 28, was damaged by flooding after overnight rainfall and has been rebuilt.

Electricity, 15 September: Dhading is restored across the district with the Jahare substation in service; Nuwakot is restored everywhere except flood-hit Betrawati, still on supply from Chapali and Balaju and still suffering low voltage; Rasuwa reaches about 90% of households, with 738 households in Uttargaya wards 1 and 2 and Gosaikunda wards 1, 2 and 3 still without supply.

Communications, 15 September: Nepal Telecom has 117 of its 120 BTS towers operational and Ncell 76 of 78. Nepal Telecom sites at Timure, Chilime Khola and Trishuli 3B are still out, as is Ncell's Timure site, while its Uttargaya-1 Tiru site is down on a power outage. Internet has been restored at Dhikure, Battar, Bidur, Chaughada, Sera, Trishuli, Galchhi, Khanikhola, Charaudi, Malekhu, Adamghat, Dhunche and Devighat, and free Wi-Fi is running at five schools and holding centres in Bidur, Rasuwa and Swayambhu.

Search and rescue, 15 September: at Chilime 150 m of the 250 m tunnel has been searched and debris fully cleared from 80 m of it, with Nepal Army, Indian Army and NDRF teams working night shifts while water is pumped out. A joint Nepal Army and Chinese DART team went about 170 m into the Langtang tunnel with a thermal drone and found nothing. At Upper Trishuli-1 a team searched 200 m into Adit-1 at Hakubeshi with no trace; with Adit-1 blocked, teams entered through Adit-3 and cleared 60 m of debris along the connecting tunnel. At Trishuli 3B, excavation about 2 m below river level has exposed the project office foundation and part of a powerhouse pillar, with Adit-1 cleared for 476 m and Adit-2 for 2.7 km, but nothing found of residential blocks A1, A2, B1, B2 or D. The 19-member Australian DART team left on Bhadra 29; seven Australian forensic personnel remain in Kathmandu.
Shelter, 19 September: 1,342 people remain in 24 holding centres - 794 in 9 centres in Rasuwa, 427 in 11 in Nuwakot and 121 in 4 in Dhading, down from 2,155 in 30 centres on 15 September.

Roads, 19 September: two-way traffic resumed at Krishnabhir on the Prithvi Highway at 06:00 on 17 September, and traffic at Jyamireghat-Chaukibhir, interrupted the previous evening, resumed the morning of 18 September; Shital Bazaar remains one lane while hard-rock blasting continues, and the proposed Fisling-to-Benighat bridge alternative is still in procurement with construction not begun. Of the 10 km Bidur-Betrawati section, 9.2 km is clear and the remaining 0.8 km, including 0.5 km of hard rock, is still being cut; foundation excavation for the Betrawati Bailey bridge has begun.

Electricity, 19 September: supply is fully restored in all areas except 46 households in Dahalfedi, ward 1, and 40 in Lingling, ward 3, of Gosaikunda Rural Municipality, Rasuwa; solar power systems are being distributed where restoring the grid will take longer.

Communications, 19 September: Nepal Telecom has 117 of 120 BTS towers operational, with Timure, Chilime Khola and Trishuli 3B still out; Ncell has service interruptions at Timure, Tiru, Gatlang and Goljung, the last two on transformer failures. 12 of 29 arranged satellite internet terminals are installed and operational, one at NDRRMA, seven in Nuwakot and four in Rasuwa.

Search and rescue, 19 September: following site inspections, the Rasuwa District Security Committee and project management stood down further search and rescue at Langtang and Chilime. At Upper Trishuli-1's Adit-3 tunnel at Hakubeshi, crews cutting steel reinforcement cleared about 2,000 m of tunnel and recovered 31 bodies trapped in a rebar-mesh structure prepared for concrete lining, on top of 6 recovered earlier from the same tunnel; 13 of the 31 were scheduled for transport to Trishuli on 20 September. Searches at Rasuwagadhi, Langtang, Chilime, Trishuli 3A and Trishuli 3B found nothing further.
